title: Medicare Advantage Star Ratings: Formula, Stakes & Strategy
summary: How CMS calculates 1-5 star ratings for Medicare Advantage plans, what the financial stakes are, and how plans manage their star strategy.

objectives.text: Explain the 5-star rating formula and its major domains
Describe the financial consequences of star rating levels for MA plans
Identify the measures with the highest weight and strategic importance

content_blocks.body:
CMS rates every Medicare Advantage and Part D plan on a 1–5 star scale, published annually on Medicare.gov. Stars serve two purposes: consumer transparency (beneficiaries can compare plans) and financial incentives (CMS pays quality bonuses to plans rated 4 stars or above).

The stakes are enormous. A plan earning 4+ stars receives a 5% bonus on its base payment rate — worth hundreds of millions of dollars annually for large plans. Plans below 3 stars for three consecutive years can be terminated from Medicare Advantage.
content_blocks.heading: Stars as a market signal and a financial lever

content_blocks.body: CMS assigns different weights to different measures — some count 3x, 4x, or 5x in the final calculation. The highest-weight measures include medication adherence for chronic conditions, care for older adults, and care transitions. Plans invest most heavily in improving these measures because the return on a star improvement is highest.
content_blocks.heading: Highest-weight measures: where plans focus

content_blocks.hint: Interview a Medicare Advantage quality director about which star measures are hardest to move, what interventions have worked, and how the star program has changed plan behavior. Recommended: 8–10 minutes.
